principles: Preserve originals: every operation reads inputs read-only; repairs, patches, conversions and extractions write only to new user-specified output paths.
Evidence first: results separate observed facts (offsets, bytes, hashes, parser output) from interpretation and hypothesis, each with confidence.
Authorization gate: dual-use analysis (malware triage, anti-analysis indicators, license/integrity logic, secrets material) requires an explicit purpose from the allowed list.
Approval gate: any writing repair, binary patch, or repack-over-existing requires --approve; dry-run is the default and shows the exact change plan.

No arbitrary execution: no shell=True, no eval of artifact content, no network access, no dynamic execution of analyzed artifacts. External tools run only from the configured allowlist with fixed argument templates and timeouts.
Dynamic analysis (debuggers, tracers, emulators, device tools) is plan-only: the tool generates bounded runbooks and checks tool availability but never launches target programs.

secrets.reason: Secrets scanning is defensive; requires an explicit authorized purpose. Findings are redacted by default.

repair-write.reason: Writing a repaired artifact requires --approve; default is a dry-run change plan.

patch-apply.reason: Applying a binary patch requires --approve plus matching precondition hash; a .bak backup and rollback plan are produced.

repack-overwrite.reason: Repacking over an existing output path requires --approve.

external-dynamic.reason: Dynamic tools are never executed by this tool; use the generated plan in an authorized isolated environment.

redaction.secrets_findings: show rule id, offset, line, and a 6-character fingerprint only; never print full secret values
redaction.purpose_required_message: This operation is dual-use. Re-run with --purpose defensive (or interoperability/research/preservation) after confirming authorization for the artifact.

prohibited: circumvention of access controls, licensing, or DRM
network scanning or remote system interaction
